title: Children, but not language models, show accelerating returns in word learning
abstract: arXiv:2608.17120v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Children learn hundreds of words over the first years of their lives, in a process that begins slowly but quickly picks up speed. Prior models describe vocabulary growth as evidence accumulation over time. Here we show that the process is best characterized as accelerating accumulation: children learn more from each additional unit of linguistic experience than they did from the one before. In contrast to children, language models -- even those trained on child-directed speech -- do not accelerate. Instead, they show constant proportional returns on new data, consistent with scaling laws. Children learn using many orders of magnitude less training data than language models; their increasingly efficient use of their learning input is a candidate explanation.

translated_title: 儿童而非语言模型在词汇学习中表现出加速回报
translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2608.17120v1 公告类型：新 摘要：儿童在生命的最初几年里学习数百个单词，这个过程开始时缓慢，但迅速加速。先前的模型将词汇增长描述为随时间累积的证据。在这里，我们表明这一过程最好被表征为加速累积：儿童从每一额外的语言经验单位中学到的比前一个更多。与儿童相比，语言模型——即使是那些在儿童导向言语上训练的模型——并不加速。相反，它们对新数据表现出恒定的比例回报，这与缩放定律一致。儿童使用的训练数据比语言模型少几个数量级；他们对学习输入日益高效的利用是一个候选解释。
tldr: 儿童在词汇学习中表现出加速回报，而语言模型则遵循恒定比例回报，这表明儿童高效利用学习输入是关键差异。
en_tdlr: Children show accelerating returns in word learning, while language models exhibit constant proportional returns, highlighting children's efficient use of learning input as a key difference.
